summary: A 1903 wooden light on Cross Point, replaced in 1937 by the Art Moderne concrete tower that still stands, automated since 1969.

access.note: Not open to the public; Coast Guard-owned aid to navigation on a remote island.

events.note: Light-House Board first asks Congress for a light and fog signal on Mary Island

Concrete light and fog-signal building replaces the 1903 station; work began Sept 1936
Lighthouse Service passes to the Coast Guard
Automated; four crewmen at the time

notes_for_editor: Sources disagree on: customs house year (1892 NRHP, 1891 LighthouseFriends); first lighting (mid-July vs 15 July 1903); electrification (1927 NRHP, 1926 LighthouseFriends, and a 1918 Bulletin item already changing to flashing acetylene); the 1920 accident (Bulletin: helping a wrecked boat; Alaska Daily Empire: a hunting outing; LighthouseFriends names Chapman and Williams as boys aged 18 and 17, not used); what happened to the dwellings (NRHP: one razed by 1960s, rest burned 1974; LighthouseFriends: one sold 1964, one moved 1970); and the lens (NRHP: whereabouts unknown / reportedly stayed in the light; LighthouseFriends: displayed in Juneau 2005). The 1929 Bulletin item on the Fairbanks is dated by the volume only (March 7, year taken as 1929); its OCR is poor and the rescuing vessel's name is unreadable, so it is omitted. The Bulletin 1917 efficiency-flag list was read from a garbled table: the district numbers and station names were matched by position and the keeper name S. F. Shepard sits beside Mary Island. USLHS roster spans are the archive's documented spans; Scott's 1918-1921 span runs past his death in December 1920. LighthouseFriends says B. H. Lervick's father was keeper 1923-27 against the archive's 1923-1930. NRHP 'whereabouts of the Fresnel lens unknown' vs status field set to unknown. Characteristic and range omitted (no cited source read). Nomination authorship: 2005 form, owner then listed as the Coast Guard. Fact-check 2026-10-27: the customs-house passage first appears in the Board's report for fiscal 1892 (scan p. 584), repeated in 1893; the 1917 efficiency-flag table was confirmed by the Bulletin index (Shepard, keeper, Mary Island, flag, p. 250).
